2607.26825.title: From Found to Designed: Concepts as a Design Axis for Large Language Models
2607.26825.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) encode rich concept-like information, but represent it implicitly through distributed statistical associations rather than as explicit, structured, compositional concepts. Consequently, concept-level structure is typically \emph{found} rather than \emph{designed}: it is recovered after training through probing or dictionary learning, with no architectural guarantee of stability, compositionality, controllability, or alignment with human conceptual organization. We argue that concepts should instead be treated as a design axis for LLMs, and map the design space along two dimensions: the pipeline stage at which concept structure is introduced (training objective, core architecture, inference, or post-hoc interpretation), and whether that structure is internally derived from the model's own representations or grounded in external resources. This taxonomy reveals three broad patterns: inference-time approaches remain comparatively underexplored, related ideas have developed largely in isolation across pipeline stages, and externally grounded methods span the entire pipeline despite often being described under different terminology. Together, these observations motivate moving beyond recovering concept-like structure from trained models toward designing LLMs with explicit conceptual representations.
2607.26825.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）編碼了豐富的概念類信息，但通過分佈式統計關聯隱式地表示，而不是作為明確的、結構化的、組合的概念。因此，概念級結構通常是\emph{發現}而不是\emph{設計}：它是在訓練後通過探測或字典學習恢復的，並沒有穩定性、組合性、可控性或與人類概念組織對齊的架構保證。我們認為，概念應該被視為LLMs的一個設計軸，並沿著兩個維度映射設計空間：引入概念結構的管道階段（訓練目標、核心架構、推理或事後解釋），以及該結構是內部從模型自身的表示中推導出來還是基於外部資源。這一分類法揭示了三種廣泛的模式：推理時的方式相對較少被探索，相關的想法在管道階段之間大多是孤立發展的，而外部基礎的方法則跨越整個管道，儘管通常以不同的術語描述。總的來說，這些觀察促使我們超越從訓練模型中恢復概念類結構，朝著設計具有明確概念表示的LLMs邁進。
